subject: Surge safeguard — pricing model & activation options
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@optiscale.com>
Cc: Keith Moore <keith@optiscale.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Surges & pricing — first pass proposal attached

Hi Samantha / Keith,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to see the traffic profile. As discussed, I attached a first-pass "surge safeguard" proposal that tries to balance predictable unit economics with rapid short-term capacity for your spikes. High level:

- Baseline commit: covers your steady-state (we used the 90th percentile from May as the baseline).
- Surge safeguard: two activation paths — (A) automatic burst credits drawn from a pre-purchased pool at a discounted overage rate, or (B) month-to-month capped overrun reconciliation with a lower per-token discount and a capped monthly liability.
- Lead time for permanent rate-limit increases: 7 business days (engineering needs a short window to provision and route).

I put concrete numbers in the PDF but quick illustration: baseline rate $0.0012/token; pre-purchased burst credits $0.0009/token (10% discount), capped overrun pricing $0.0010/token with monthly cap at $15k. Open to adjusting numbers — wanted to get something on paper for procurement.

Attachment: surge-pricing-proposal-v1.pdf

Would you prefer a capped monthly liability or the flexibility to buy credits as-needed? If you want, we can draft a one-page amendment to add onto your existing MSA.

Best,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwood.ai]

From: Samantha Park <samantha@optiscale.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:03:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Surges & pricing — first pass proposal attached

Thanks Jasmine — the deck is clear. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we loop procurement:

1) How would the monthly cap work with sudden daily spikes (e.g., 3 high days in a month)? Is the cap applied after the month-end reconciliation or is it a hard throttle?
2) If we choose pre-purchased burst credits, do they expire? We had a month in May where we consumed ~2.4M extra tokens over baseline, which is why we want a lower price in worst-case months.
3) Can you confirm whether the 7-day activation applies to both Dedicated and Hosted routing? Our infra team is sensitive to changes that require traffic re-routing.

Also cc'ing procurement so they can see the numbers early.

—Samantha
Samantha Park

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Surges & pricing — internal — negotiation posture

Jaz — quick thoughts on posture before you reply to OptiScale:

- Option A (preferred for predictability): Pre-purchased burst credits that expire after 12 months. Price = baseline * 0.75 (25% discount) for credits sold in 100k token blocks; minimum purchase $5k. This avoids surprise monthly caps and locks in revenue.

- Option B (customer-friendly): Monthly overrun true-up with a soft cap. Example: overrun priced at baseline * 0.90 (10% discount) up to $12k/month; any usage beyond that triggers rate-limit throttling or manual authorization. We can offer a 1-time waiver for May (as a good will) but set expectation on future months.

- Activation: keep 7 business days for permanent increases, but offer a 24–48 hour emergency short-term burst (engineering-approved) that routes to spare capacity for a fee (higher per-token surcharge) — use only once per invoice month unless pre-approved.

- Legal/procurement asks: If they want Option A, finance needs an SKU and an amendment template. If Option B, we need a liability cap line in the amendment and sign-off on throttling behavior.

Putting numbers in a one-pager will help procurement choose. Happy to let Jaz present both and recommend Option A for Redwood.

-Adi

---

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@optiscale.com>, Keith Moore <keith@optiscale.com>, procurement@optiscale.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Surges & pricing — updated offer + activation options

Hi Samantha / Keith — thanks for the questions. Quick replies and a short revised offer below. Full one-page amendment attached for procurement.

Q1 (monthly cap vs throttle): The cap is applied at monthly reconciliation (soft cap) — we do NOT hard-throttle mid-month unless usage exceeds the explicit emergency threshold. We will surface daily burn alerts at 80%/90% so you can opt to buy credits early.

Q2 (credits expiry): Pre-purchased burst credits expire in 12 months. We can sell credits in 100k increments.

Q3 (activation & routing): 7 business days for permanent rate increases for both Hosted and Dedicated routing. Emergency short-term bursts (up to 48 hours) can be activated within 24–48 hours subject to engineering availability and a one-time surcharge of 30% on the negotiated burst rate.

Revised commercial (two paths):

- Path A — Pre-purchased burst credits (recommended)
  * Credits: sell in 100k token blocks, 12-month expiry.
  * Pricing: $0.0009/token (25% discount off baseline list we provided).
  * Minimum purchase: $5,000 equivalent (≈5.55M tokens at this price).

- Path B — Monthly overrun reconciliation with soft cap
  * Overrun price: $0.0010/token (10% discount).
  * Monthly soft cap: $12,000 (Redwood absorbs overruns up to that amount; anything beyond requires manual approval or we throttle).

Additional concessions: one-time May goodwill credit of $6,500 if we finalize amendment by 20 Jun.

Attachments: amendment_one-pager.pdf, amendment_sku.csv

Next steps: if procurement gives a PO number we’ll prepare an amendment + invoice (Path A requires SKU + PO; Path B can proceed with an amendment to existing MSA). Also including a DocuSign link if you'd rather sign online.

Best,
Jasmine 
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwood.ai]

Jasmine — appreciate the clarity and the May goodwill credit offer. Procurement prefers Path A (pre-purchased credits) to avoid month-to-month surprises. They asked for the SKU and a draft PO — looping them here.

We'd like the credits to be available immediately after PO processing and not require additional engineering changes on our side beyond the 7-business-day routing note — is that feasible? If not, we accept the 24–48 hour emergency burst path until routing completes.

Procurement: PO number TBC, please let us know the SKU and the final DocuSign link.

—Samantha
